info.name: MAI_ISHA API
info.description:
MAI_ISHA Fashion & Beauty Sphere — Laravel API (Sanctum SPA cookie auth, GBP e-commerce).

## Before you run this

1. Start the API: `cd backend && php artisan serve` (or the Docker Compose stack — switch the `base_url` variable to `http://localhost:8080` if so).
2. Make sure the database is migrated and seeded: `php artisan migrate:fresh --seed`. This collection's example bodies assume the seeded demo data:
   - Admin: `admin@maiisha.test` / `password`
   - Customer: `customer@maiisha.test` / `password`
   - Discount code: `WELCOME10` (10% off, no usage limit)
   - ~14 seeded products across the 9 PRD categories, each with 1+ variants
3. Import both files in this folder: this collection, and the `MAI_ISHA - Local.postman_environment.json` environment (or the Docker one). Select the environment in Postman's top-right environment picker before sending anything.

## How auth works here

The API uses **Laravel Sanctum's cookie/session auth**, the same as the real Next.js frontend — there is no bearer token to paste in. Postman's cookie jar handles this automatically once you run **00 - Setup → Get CSRF Cookie**, and this collection keeps the CSRF token fresh after every request via a collection-level script (see below). Just run requests top-to-bottom within a folder and it behaves like a logged-in browser session.

## Folder order matters

Folders are numbered in the order they're meant to run — each builds on state (cookies + collection variables) left behind by the one before it:

1. **00 - Setup** — always run this first (per environment / per Postman session restart)
2. **01 - Auth** — registers a fresh, uniquely-emailed customer and logs them in
3. **02 - Catalogue (Public)** — no auth needed; also harvests a product/variant to buy
4. **03 - Cart** — adds/updates/removes items using the harvested variant(s)
5. **04 - My Addresses** — creates the delivery address checkout will use
6. **05 - Checkout** — previews totals (incl. `WELCOME10`), then places the order
7. **06 - My Orders** — reads back the order just placed
8. **07 - Admin - Auth** — logs in as the seeded admin (replaces the customer session)
9. **08 through 12 - Admin - \*** — dashboard, categories, products/variants/images, order fulfilment, discount codes
10. **13 - Webhooks (Reference)** — not directly runnable from Postman (see its description) — documents the Stripe webhook contract instead

You can also run the whole collection via **Collection Runner** top-to-bottom and it will tell a coherent story end-to-end, with `pm.test()` assertions on every request.

## Notes

- All money fields are integers in **pence** (GBP only, per PRD Phase 1 scope).
- Re-running **01 - Auth → Register** always creates a brand-new account (its email uses `{{$timestamp}}`), so the whole collection is safely re-runnable without unique-constraint clashes.
- The Stripe keys in `backend/.env` are placeholders by default, so **05 - Checkout → Place Order** will correctly fail at the payment-gateway step with a clean 422 ("We could not start payment") rather than a raw Stripe error — that's expected until real Stripe test keys are configured, not a bug.

variable.description: Paste manually from storage/logs/laravel.log (search 'Reset Password:') after running Auth → Forgot Password.

exec: // Sanctum's EnsureFrontendRequestsAreStateful only turns on session/CSRF
// middleware when Origin/Referer matches SANCTUM_STATEFUL_DOMAINS — it's a
// plain string match, not real CORS enforcement, so a non-browser client
// like Postman just needs to send the same header a browser would.
// Laravel re-issues a fresh XSRF-TOKEN cookie on every response as long as
// the session is alive, so just keep the collection variable in sync after
// every single request — no need to re-fetch the csrf-cookie endpoint.

item.name: 00 - Setup
item.description: Run once per Postman session (or whenever cookies get cleared) before anything else.

request.description: Sanctum's SPA bootstrap endpoint. Sets the XSRF-TOKEN and session cookies Postman needs for every request after this one — mirrors exactly what the real Next.js frontend does on load.
Creates a brand-new account (unique email each run via {{$timestamp}}, so this collection is safely re-runnable) and logs it straight in — the rest of the customer journey uses this session.

Demonstrates the login endpoint by logging back into the account Register just created (safe — doesn't switch the active journey to a different identity). To try the pre-seeded demo account instead, swap the body for customer@maiisha.test / password — just note that derails the rest of this folder's story, since it becomes the active session.
Confirms the cookie session is authenticated as the expected user.
Updates the {{customer_password}} variable too, so any later request in this folder that re-authenticates keeps working.

exec: pm.test('Response is a generic message (no email enumeration)', () => {

request.description: Always returns the same generic message whether or not the email is registered, by design. Locally (MAIL_MAILER=log) the actual reset link — including the token — is written to backend/storage/logs/laravel.log. Copy the token from there into the {{reset_token}} collection variable to try 'Reset Password' below.

exec: pm.test('Skipped: no reset_token set — see request description', () => pm.expect(true).to.be.true);

request.description: Requires a real token from storage/logs/laravel.log (set it in the {{reset_token}} collection variable first) — the token can't be captured automatically since it only ever leaves the server via email/log, by design. Without it this will correctly 422.

item.name: 02 - Catalogue (Public)
item.description: No authentication required — these also work from an incognito browser tab or curl with no cookies at all.

exec: pm.test('Returns the 9 PRD top-level categories', () => pm.expect(data.length).to.eql(9));

request.description: Top-level categories with their subcategories nested under `children`.

exec: pm.test('Products have at least one variant each', () => {

request.description: Harvests the first two products' opening variant into {{variant_id}} / {{second_variant_id}} for the Cart folder.
All available query params are listed here (some disabled) so you can toggle whichever combination you want to try.

What a shopper can narrow the current listing by: sorted `sizes` (S, M, L… then natural order for the rest) and `colours`, the `price` range (in pence, on the **sale** price), `on_sale_count`, and top-level `categories` with product counts. Scope it with `category` and/or `search`; add `on_sale=1` for the sale page.

exec: pm.test('products carry sale fields', () => body.data.forEach(p => { pm.expect(p).to.have.property('compare_at_price_pence'); pm.expect(p).to.have.property('sale'); }));

request.description: Filters combine (AND). `brand` takes one or more brand slugs, comma-separated. `size` and `colour` take several comma-separated values and one variant must match all of them; `min_price` / `max_price` are pence and act on the price the customer pays (the sale price while a sale is live); `in_stock=1` and `on_sale=1` are switches; `sort` is `latest` (default) | `price_asc` | `price_desc` | `best_selling` | `discount` (biggest saving). Searching is case-insensitive.

exec: pm.test('each live sale has a label and no admin fields', () => sales.forEach(s => { pm.expect(s).to.have.property('label'); pm.expect(s).to.not.have.property('is_active'); }));

request.description: The sales running right now — what the storefront's announcement banner and Sale page are built from. Only shopper-facing fields; nothing admin-side. A weekday-limited sale (a "Monday deal") only appears on its days, UK time.

exec: pm.test('brands have a slug and a product count', () => pm.response.json().data.forEach(b => { pm.expect(b).to.have.property('slug'); pm.expect(b.products_count).to.be.above(0); }));

request.description: Live brands that have something to buy, ordered by `sort_order` then name, each with its browsable `products_count`. A hidden brand, or one with no browsable products, isn't listed.

exec: pm.test('Status is 200 or 404 if the variable is unset', () => pm.expect([200, 404]).to.include(pm.response.code));

request.description: Set `brand_slug` from List Brands. A hidden or unknown brand is a 404. List its products with `GET /api/products?brand={{brand_slug}}`.

item.name: 03 - Cart
item.description: Cart is session-backed even for guests (FR-6) — but running these after '01 - Auth' ties it to the logged-in customer instead, exactly like a real browser.

`country` must be a 2-letter ISO code (e.g. GB), not free text — this is the mistake the frontend's first draft made.

item.name: Create a Second Address (for Delete demo)

request.description: Deletes the throwaway 'Work' address, not the default one Checkout uses.
No discount code — baseline totals for what's currently in the cart.
Uses the pre-seeded WELCOME10 code (10% off, no usage limit). Deliberately sent lowercase to demonstrate matching is case-insensitive.

exec: pm.test('Fails cleanly at the payment gateway (expected with placeholder Stripe keys)', () => {

console.warn('Place Order stopped at Stripe as expected — order_id was NOT captured. Set real Stripe test keys in backend/.env to get past this, or grab an order_id manually from the DB to continue into 06 - My Orders / Admin - Orders.');

request.description: Reserves stock and creates the order (status `pending_payment`) *before* talking to Stripe, then requests a PaymentIntent. With the placeholder STRIPE_KEY/STRIPE_SECRET shipped in .env.example, this correctly 422s at the payment-gateway step and cleanly releases the reserved stock — that's the intended failure path, not a bug. Drop in real Stripe test keys to see it succeed all the way to a `client_secret`.

exec: pm.test('Skipped: no order_id (Place Order stopped at Stripe) — see 05 - Checkout', () => pm.expect(true).to.be.true);

item.name: 07 - Admin - Auth
item.description: Logging in here replaces the active cookie session with the admin's — everything from this folder onward runs as the admin, not the customer from folders 01-06.

request.description: Order/revenue totals only count paid statuses (placed/processing/shipped/out_for_delivery/delivered) — a pending_payment order from an incomplete checkout won't show up here or in revenue_pence. `revenue_growth_percent` compares this calendar month's paid revenue to last month's (null with no prior-month baseline yet). `daily_revenue` is a zero-filled 14-day series for a trend chart.
Unlike the public /api/categories endpoint, this is a flat list (no is_active-style filtering) intended for a management table, not storefront nav.
`slug` is optional — omit it (as here) to have it auto-generated from `name`.

exec: pm.test('Status is 409 once a product exists in it', () => {

request.description: Run this BEFORE '10 - Admin - Products' and it succeeds (200) since the category is still empty. Run it AFTER creating 'Golden Hour Maxi Dress' in that folder and it correctly 409s instead of silently cascade-deleting the product — categories with products can't be deleted until they're reassigned or removed.
Unlike the public catalogue, this also returns inactive/out-of-stock products — a management view, not a storefront view.

body.raw:
{
    "category_id": {{admin_category_id}},
    "name": "Golden Hour Maxi Dress",
    "description": "Flowing maxi dress in a rich gold tone — part of the Summer Collection.",
    "price_pence": 8999,
    "is_active": true,
    "is_featured": true,
    "hide_when_out_of_stock": false
}

request.description: `price_pence` is the base price shown when a variant has no `price_override_pence` of its own. `hide_when_out_of_stock` (FR-23) defaults to `false` — an out-of-stock product still shows on the storefront marked "out of stock" unless set `true`. Uses the category created in '09 - Admin - Categories'.

body.raw:
{
    "category_id": {{admin_category_id}},
    "name": "Golden Hour Maxi Dress",
    "description": "Flowing maxi dress in a rich gold tone — now 10% more golden.",
    "price_pence": 9499,
    "is_active": true,
    "is_featured": true,
    "hide_when_out_of_stock": false
}

request.description: `price_override_pence` is omitted — this variant inherits the product's price_pence (9499). Set it to override just this variant's price (e.g. a size that costs more).

This is also the endpoint for stock adjustments (FR-22) — it's a full replace, not a partial patch, so re-send every field (sku/size/colour/stock_quantity all required) even when you only mean to change the stock count.

formdata.description: Select any local image file — required, max 5MB.

formdata.value: Model wearing the Golden Hour Maxi Dress

formdata.description: Optional (FR-3). Ties this photo to a variant colour — Product::imageFor() matches it case-insensitively against the selected variant's colour on the storefront, cart and order history, falling back to the product's first photo when no colour matches.

request.description: Postman can't ship a binary file inside a shared collection export — click into the `image` form field and choose any local image before sending this request.

request.description: Safe even if the variant is referenced by past orders — order line items snapshot their own product_name/sku/price at purchase time, so deleting the live variant doesn't touch order history.
Run this last in the folder — deletes the product created above, which then lets '09 - Admin - Categories → Delete Category' succeed if you re-run it.
Adds `quantity` to the variant's current stock (atomic — never overwrites). Fires back-in-stock emails when a sold-out variant returns.

item.name: 11 - Admin - Orders
item.description: Uses {{order_id}} from '05 - Checkout'. If that stopped at the Stripe placeholder-key step (the expected default), order_id won't be set — see that folder's description for how to proceed anyway.

query.description: placed | processing | shipped | out_for_delivery | delivered | cancelled | pending_payment

request.description: Matches order number, customer name or email.

pm.test('Skipped: no order_id — see 05 - Checkout', () => pm.expect(true).to.be.true);

request.description: Note: the API doesn't enforce a strict status state-machine (e.g. it won't stop you jumping straight from pending_payment to shipped) — that's intentional, so admins can correct mistakes, but it means Postman can walk the full lifecycle here without needing a real Stripe webhook to fire first.

request.description: Auto-creates a shipment record (via the ShippingProvider interface — a logging stand-in until a real courier aggregator is contracted, per PRD §9) and fires the email+SMS 'shipped' notification (FR-18). Check backend/storage/logs/laravel.log to see both.

item.name: Update Order Status → Out for Delivery

exec: pm.test('Skipped: no order_id — see 05 - Checkout', () => pm.expect(true).to.be.true);

request.description: Fires the email+SMS 'out for delivery' notification (FR-9/FR-18) and updates the shipment's status. Run after 'Shipped' to see it stack in backend/storage/logs/laravel.log.

exec: pm.test('Skipped: no order_id — see 05 - Checkout', () => pm.expect(true).to.be.true);
pm.test('200 refunded, 422 no succeeded payment, or 502 gateway failure', () => pm.expect([200,422,502]).to.include(pm.response.code));

request.description: Refunds the whole payment via Stripe, then restocks, frees the discount code and cancels the order. 422 when there is no succeeded payment; 502 leaves the order untouched.
Includes a usages_count for each code.

Sent lowercase deliberately — codes are always normalised to uppercase on save, and matched case-insensitively at checkout. `type` is `percentage` (value = percentage points, capped at 100) or `fixed` (value = pence off).
Deliberately invalid — demonstrates the validation guard against a nonsensical >100% discount.
This is a soft-deactivate (is_active → false), never a hard delete — preserves usage history for reporting.

exec: pm.test('stored as a fixed 500p code', () => { pm.expect(code.type).to.eql('fixed'); pm.expect(code.value).to.eql(500); pm.expect(code.code).to.eql('POSTMAN5'); });

request.description: A promo code is either a percentage off or a FIXED amount off. For `type: "fixed"` the `value` is pence (500 = £5.00 off); checkout never takes more than the subtotal off. Percentage values are capped at 100, fixed amounts aren't.

item.name: 13 - Admin - Brands
item.description: Brands (labels) for products: shoppers can filter by brand and browse each brand's page, and a sale can target a whole brand. A brand that still has products can't be deleted (409) — switch it off with `is_active: false` instead, which hides its page, filter and label while its products stay on sale. The slug is set from the name at creation and does not change when the brand is renamed. Logo upload is `POST /api/admin/brands/{id}/logo` (multipart, field `logo`, image up to 2 MB) — send it from Postman's form-data tab; it isn't part of this run so the collection stays runnable without a file. Run 07 - Admin - Auth first.

exec: pm.test('each brand has a product count', () => pm.response.json().data.forEach(b => pm.expect(b).to.have.property('products_count')));

request.description: Every brand, hidden ones included, with `products_count`, ordered by `sort_order` then name.

exec: pm.test('slug is derived from the name', () => pm.expect(brand.slug).to.match(/^postman-label(-\d+)?$/));

request.description: The slug comes from the name; a name that would collide gets `-2`, `-3`… instead of failing.

exec: pm.test('name changed, slug did not', () => { const b = pm.response.json().data; pm.expect(b.name).to.eql('Postman Label (renamed)'); pm.expect(b.slug).to.match(/^postman-label/); });

request.description: Renaming doesn't move the brand's URL.
Only allowed while the brand has no products (otherwise 409). To check the guard, assign the brand to a product first (`brand_id` on Update Product).

item.name: 14 - Admin - Sales
item.description: Seasonal and recurring automatic price reductions (Christmas, Ileya, "Monday deals"). Sales need no code: while one is live, everything it covers is cheaper in listings, the product page, cart, checkout and the order itself. The best price wins where sales overlap (they don't stack); a discount code still applies on top. Dates are read as **UK time**; `active_weekdays` are ISO days (1 = Monday … 7 = Sunday), null = every day. Sales are MANUAL by default: `is_active` is the switch (Activate / Deactivate), and a sale with no dates and no weekdays is live exactly while it is active — the way Christmas, Ileya and Black Friday work. Dates and weekdays are optional extras. Run 07 - Admin - Auth first.

exec: pm.test('each sale reports a status', () => pm.response.json().data.forEach(s => pm.expect(['live','scheduled','ended','inactive']).to.include(s.status)));

request.description: Newest first, every status, with the categories/products each covers. `status` is `live`, `scheduled` (not started yet, or between its weekdays), `ended` or `inactive` (switched off).

exec: pm.test('label is derived from the discount', () => pm.expect(sale.discount_label).to.eql('10% off'));

request.description: A recurring Monday deal: no dates, just `active_weekdays: [1]`. For a dated sale send `starts_at` / `ends_at` as `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm` (UK time). To limit it, send `applies_to: "selected"` with any mix of `category_ids` (lines — subcategories included), `brand_ids` and `product_ids`. A sale with nothing chosen yet is a valid draft.

body.raw:
{
    "name": "Monday Deals (Postman)",
    "description": "Every Monday: 10% off",
    "type": "percentage",
    "value": 10,
    "applies_to": "all",
    "starts_at": null,
    "ends_at": null,
    "active_weekdays": [
        1
    ],
    "is_active": true
}

request.description: Includes `starts_at_local` / `ends_at_local` — the same instants as UK wall-clock time, which is what a date-time form field reads and writes.
A full replace (send every field). Prices across the shop change the moment it's saved.

body.raw:
{
    "name": "Monday Deals (Postman, updated)",
    "description": "Every Monday: 10% off",
    "type": "percentage",
    "value": 15,
    "applies_to": "all",
    "starts_at": null,
    "ends_at": null,
    "active_weekdays": [
        1
    ],
    "is_active": true
}

request.description: A percentage sale is capped at 99% — 100% off would create £0 lines the payment provider can't charge.

body.raw:
{
    "name": "Monday Deals (Postman)",
    "description": "Every Monday: 10% off",
    "type": "percentage",
    "value": 100,
    "applies_to": "all",
    "starts_at": null,
    "ends_at": null,
    "active_weekdays": [
        1
    ],
    "is_active": true
}

request.description: Never a hard delete: it switches the sale off (`is_active: false`), so a past campaign keeps its name in analytics. Switch it back on with Update Sale.
A seasonal campaign the way it's meant to work: no dates, saved as a DRAFT (`is_active: false`), covering a line, a brand and (optionally) products. Nothing changes in the shop until it is activated.

body.raw:
{
    "name": "Black Friday (Postman)",
    "description": "Our biggest deals of the year",
    "type": "percentage",
    "value": 30,
    "applies_to": "selected",
    "category_ids": [{{admin_category_id}}],
    "brand_ids": [{{admin_brand_id}}],
    "product_ids": [],
    "starts_at": null,
    "ends_at": null,
    "active_weekdays": null,
    "is_active": false
}

request.description: Switches the sale on: for a manual sale it is live straight away and stays live until Deactivate. A dated or weekly sale becomes eligible and runs on its own dates/days.

item.name: 15 - Admin - Analytics
item.description: Numbers for the admin Analytics page, for a chosen period against the equal-length period before it. Only paid orders count as sales. "Days" are UK days, not UTC.

exec: pm.test('money reconciles', () => { const m = r.money; pm.expect(m.list_price_pence - m.sale_savings_pence - m.code_discounts_pence + m.shipping_pence).to.eql(m.total_pence); });

request.description: `range` = `7d` | `30d` (default) | `90d` | `12m` | `ytd` | `custom` (then `from` and `to`, `YYYY-MM-DD`, up to two years). The time series is zero-filled and grouped by day, then week (past 62 days), then month (past ~6 months); each bucket also carries the previous period's revenue for an overlay. `change_percent` is null when there's nothing earlier to compare against.
An end date in the future is clamped to today.
The period's paid orders as a CSV for bookkeeping / the VAT return: amounts in pounds, dates in UK time. Customer-supplied text is neutralised against spreadsheet formula injection.

item.name: 16 - Admin - Notifications
item.description: The notification bell's feed — synthesised from real state (new paid orders, low/out-of-stock variants, checkouts stuck on pending payment for 2+ hours, sales ending within a day), not a stored table. "Unread" is one per-admin cursor (`users.notifications_read_at`), not a flag per item, so marking read clears everything up to now in one call. A sale ending soon is shown but never counts toward the unread badge (it's a standing heads-up, not a one-off event). Run 07 - Admin - Auth first.

request.description: Sorted newest first, capped at 30. Each item's `id` is a stable string (`order-12`, `stock-5`, `sale-3`, `stale-9`) suited to a React key. `unread_count` only counts countable types (orders, stock, stale checkouts) — never sales ending soon.
Sets the cursor to now — every notification up to this instant is read; anything created after (even a second later) is unread again on the next fetch.

item.name: 17 - Admin - Customers
item.description: Customer accounts (role=customer only — an admin account is never listed or messageable here, and is a 404 if tried by id). `orders_count`/`total_spent_pence` count paid orders only; a customer with three abandoned checkouts and no purchases shows £0. Run 07 - Admin - Auth first.

exec: pm.test('paginated with order stats per customer', () => body.data.forEach(c => { pm.expect(c).to.have.property('orders_count'); pm.expect(c).to.have.property('total_spent_pence'); }));

request.description: Search by name or email with `search`.
CSV of customers matching `search`: name, email, phone, joined, paid orders, total spent.
Includes the customer's saved addresses.
Paid and unpaid alike, newest first — unlike the dashboard/analytics figures, which count paid orders only.
A one-off email, not an order-status notification (see OrderNotifier) — it never texts them, and needs no order/status to send.

item.name: 18 - Webhooks (Reference)
item.description: Not directly runnable from Postman — Stripe cryptographically signs every webhook request (see StripeWebhookController), and a hand-crafted Postman request has no way to produce a valid signature for STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET. This request documents the contract instead. To actually exercise it locally, use the Stripe CLI: `stripe listen --forward-to localhost:8000/api/webhooks/stripe`, then `stripe trigger payment_intent.succeeded`.

exec: pm.test('Correctly rejects an unsigned request', () => pm.response.to.have.status(400));

request.description: Sending this as-is (no Stripe-Signature header) correctly gets rejected with 400 'Invalid signature' — that's the expected, secure behaviour being demonstrated, not something to fix. Handled events: `payment_intent.succeeded` (marks the order placed, sends the placed notification) and `payment_intent.payment_failed` (cancels the order, restocks items, removes any discount-code usage record).
